title: Error
description:
The shape of an error body. This is the repository's first error schema; before it, every non-2xx in the contract was `description:` prose with no `content:`.

It models EXACTLY what the API emits today (#427 W6, decision D4) — no aspirational fields. `detail` is what FastAPI's `HTTPException` handler produces and is the only guaranteed member; `request_id` and `reason` are the two additions the store-unavailable 503 carries (#427 W2a).

WHY `detail` HAS NO TYPE. It is a string almost everywhere, an ARRAY for FastAPI's own 422 validation body, and an OBJECT in exactly one place — the `owner_quota_exceeded` 409, which returns `{error, owned, limit, message}` so a caller can act on the numbers without parsing prose. Constraining it to a string would make this schema wrong for two shapes the API already ships. It is `{}` on purpose, not by omission.

WHY NO `store` FIELD. The 503 body names the failing store inside `detail`'s sentence and nothing consumes a separate field: the UI branches on `reason` alone. Under `additionalProperties: false` a property modelled but never emitted is harmless, but a property emitted but never modelled is a conformance failure — so this schema stays at what ships. Adding `store` later is additive and breaks nothing.

WHERE IT IS WIRED. `content:` references this schema only from the 503 responses of POST /v1/query and POST /v1/retrieve — the responses #427's incident produced. It is deliberately NOT retro-applied to every 4xx: that would be a large audit of bodies nobody has a complaint about. Every error body in the API was checked against this shape when it was written (including the hand-built 411/413 from the upload guard, which bypasses the router entirely) and all of them validate, so widening later is a documentation change rather than an implementation one.

detail.description: What went wrong. A human-readable sentence for nearly every error; an array of per-field validation errors for a 422; an object for the `owner_quota_exceeded` 409. Deliberately untyped — see the schema description. This is SERVER PROSE and may name internal hosts, collections and settings: the reference UI never renders it to a user (see ErrorBanner's no-echo rule), it is for operators and for callers that log it.

request_id.description: The correlation id for the request that failed — the same value the `X-Request-Id` response header carries, and the `rid=` on every log line the request produced. Redundant with the header on purpose: a header does not survive a user copy-pasting the JSON body into a ticket. Present on the store-unavailable 503; absent from bodies produced by FastAPI's own `HTTPException` handler, which is why it is optional rather than required.

reason.description:
Machine-readable failure class for a store-unavailable 503, from `StoreUnavailable.kind`. The distinction is load-bearing for what a user should be told: `timeout` means we CONNECTED and the search was too slow, so a retry hits a warm read and often succeeds within seconds; `unreachable` means we never reached the store at all, so a retry probably will not help; `error` means the store answered unhappily. A `ConnectTimeout` is classified `unreachable`, not `timeout`, precisely so the UI does not promise a warm second read that will not happen.

Absent from the other 503 causes on the same endpoints (authorization store fail-closed, a dormant or restoring collection, tenant at capacity), which are `detail`-only. A consumer must treat an absent OR unrecognised value as the conservative case.
